title: Isolation raises vs limps
summary: Do not auto-call behind limpers from late position. canonical_lesson:
# DAILY MTT EDGE #001
**Date:** Saturday 29 August 2026
**Category:** Preflop Fundamentals
**Topic:** Isolation raises vs limps
**Hook:** Stop auto-calling behind limpers. When they limp, think isolation first.
**Status:** Draft for review
**Main concept:** Do not flat behind limpers from late position as a default. Isolate so you play heads-up in position against a weak, capped range, unless stack depth, position, or table type says otherwise.
**Example:** 32bb, BTN Aâ™  Jâ™£ vs a typical UTG limp
**Takeaway:** A limp is an invitation to isolate, not an invitation to call.

---

## Today's Edge

In low and mid-stakes online MTTs, someone limps. You look down at a playable hand on the cutoff or button and click call. It feels cheap. It feels like you are keeping the pot small. It is usually one of the most expensive cheap calls you can make.

When you flat behind a limp, two things happen at once. The blinds now have a price they almost cannot refuse, so you go three- or four-way. And the limper's weak, capped range suddenly has the right odds to continue. Ace-Jack, King-Queen, and medium pairs wanted a heads-up pot in position. The call turns them into bloated multiway hands.

Isolation raising is how you take the pot you actually wanted. A raise of about 3.5â€“4x, plus one extra big blind per extra limper, often folds out the blinds, puts the limper to a decision with junk, and leaves you heads-up in position. That is where your skill edge lives. Size up if the table is sticky. Size down a little if the blinds are tight and already folding too much.

You do not need a premium to isolate from late position at 25â€“40bb. Suited broadways, strong offsuit broadways, medium pairs, and decent suited connectors are all candidates. The raise is not "I have a big hand." The raise is "I am not letting this limp build a four-way pot."

The call behind a limp is not pot control. It is an invitation to the field.

## Why It Works

**The limper is capped.** In these games, most players raise their strong hands and limp their speculative and leftover hands. That is not always true, but it is the population default. When you isolate, you are raising an uncapped range into a range that is short on premiums.

**The dead money is real.** At 30bb with a big-blind ante, the blinds, ante, and limp are a meaningful chunk of a starting stack. Taking that down preflop is a good outcome, not a missed flop. Fold equity here is part of the value of the hand, not a bonus.

**Multiway is a penalty for the hands you most want to isolate with.** Ace-Jack offsuit is a fine heads-up-in-position hand. It is a miserable four-way hand. Same for King-Queen, Ace-Ten, and many medium pairs. The call behind donates that difference. The raise collects it.

**You keep initiative and position if they call.** Limp-call ranges miss a lot of flops and overfold in low- and mid-stakes fields. You get to c-bet a lot of dry and semi-dry boards. You can also check back some low connected boards. You cannot do either of those well four ways.

## Example Spot

- Blinds: 200 / 400 with a 400 big-blind ante
- Effective stack: 32bb (12,800)
- Hero: Button with Aâ™  Jâ™£
- UTG (32bb, unknown, typical low-stakes rec, has limped a few times already) limps
- MP folds, CO folds
- Small blind ~28bb, big blind ~40bb, both unknown
- Action: UTG limps. Action on you.
- Decision: call or isolate?

This is a very common 25â€“40bb online MTT spot. The field limps, the button has a playable offsuit broadway, and the automatic click is call.

## Decision Analysis

Ace-Jack offsuit on the button, 32bb, one limp in front.

Calling 400 looks like a 1bb decision. It is not. That call prices in two blinds and turns AJ into a four-way hand. On many flops you will check back because you have no idea who has what. On other flops you will fire into three players and get called in two spots. Neither is the pot this hand wanted.

Raising to 1,600 (4x) changes the shape of the hand. The blinds now have to call a real raise, not complete cheaply. UTG has to continue with a limp range that is mostly speculative and leftover. If they fold, you pick up the blinds, ante, and limp without a flop. If UTG calls and the blinds fold, you are heads-up in position with the betting lead.

If UTG three-bets, especially a large one, Ace-Jack offsuit at 32bb is usually a fold unless you have a specific read that this player three-bets light over limps. That line is rare at these stakes. Isolating does not mean you have to continue if the limper wakes up with a real hand.

After a limp-call, treat most dry flops as c-bet territory against this player type. Check back some low, connected, or monotone boards where their limp-call range connects and your offsuit broadway does not.

## The Mistake

The common mistake is not "calling with 72 offsuit." It is calling with a hand that looks playable.

Call 400 to see a flop. The small blind completes. The big blind checks. Four ways, more than 2,000 in the middle, Ace-Jack offsuit. Flop comes 8â™¥ 7â™¥ 6â™£ or Kâ™  9â™¦ 4â™£ and you have no clean plan. You check back a flop you would have c-bet heads-up. Or you barrel into three players and run into a calling station.

Two related mistakes show up in the same spot:

- Isolating too small, like 2.2x, so the blinds still have a price and you get the multiway pot anyway.
- Isolating from early position, or with junk, into a table that never folds. Then you inflate a pot you cannot win often enough.

The first mistake is the one that burns the most chips in these games: the "cheap" call with a decent hand.

## The Better Play

Raise to 1,600. That is 4x into this ante structure, with one limper.

You often fold out the blinds. You isolate a weak, capped range. You keep position. If UTG calls, you still have the betting lead. If they fold, you take the dead money. Against a calling station, size up to 4.5â€“5x so the blinds are less likely to tag along. Against tight blinds who already overfold, 3.5x can be enough.

This is not a rule that Ace-Jack always raises. It is the default in this position, at this depth, against this player type. The raise is how you choose the pot.

## When To Use It / When Not To

**Use the isolation raise when:**
- You are in late position (cutoff or button), or sometimes small blind versus a limp
- Effective stacks are about 20â€“50bb, where fold equity still matters and postflop is still playable
- There are one or two limpers, not a parade
- The blinds can still fold
- Your hand plays well heads-up in position and poorly multiway (strong and medium broadways, medium pairs, decent suited connectors)

**Do not auto-isolate when:**
- Aggressive players are still to act behind you. Wide isolation from the hijack or cutoff gets much worse when the button or blinds squeeze a lot. You are bloating a pot you will often have to fold. Tighten, or just limp behind / fold the medium stuff.
- Stacks are 12â€“15bb. Prefer a tighter shove range over a small isolation that leaves you with a tiny remaining stack.
- The table never folds. Size up with hands that can play a raised pot, and fold the speculative stuff instead of iso-raising 76s into three calling stations.
- You have a specific read that this player open-limps premiums. That is rare in these games. If it is true, Ace-Jack is a fold or a call, not a raise.
- Several players have already limped and an aggressive player is still to act. Isolating into a squeeze is how a "standard iso" turns into a disaster. Tighter.

**Sizing, not slogans:**
- Typical rec table: 3.5â€“4x, plus 1bb per extra limper
- Sticky table: 4.5â€“5x
- Tight blinds: 3â€“3.5x can be enough
- Bigger antes make isolation more attractive, because there is more dead money

## One Thing To Remember

A limp is an invitation to isolate, not an invitation to call.

Before you auto-raise, check three things: Are you last to act or close to it? Are stacks still in the 20â€“50bb band? If someone is still behind you, do they squeeze? If the first two are yes and nobody dangerous is waiting, isolate. If not, you need a different plan.

---

## Caption (draft)

Someone limps. You look down at AJ on the button. Auto-calling feels cheap.

It usually isn't. That call prices in the blinds and turns a playable heads-up hand into a family pot. Think isolation first from late position at 25â€“40bb. Size up if they never fold. Get out if they three-bet large. Tighten if an aggressive player behind can squeeze.

Save this one for your next MTT.
